surface_name: Supabase Data API and row level security
title: Anyone with your Supabase publishable or anon key can read and write a table that has RLS off
symptoms: Rows can be read through the Data API with only the project URL and the publishable or anon key, no sign-in
Rows can be inserted, changed or deleted by requests your app never made
The table shows RLS disabled while your app ships the key in its browser code, as it is meant to
cause: The publishable key (the legacy anon key) is meant to be public, so it only protects data when Row Level Security is on. A table in an exposed schema, such as public, without RLS is readable and writable by any role with a grant on it, and on existing projects new tables in public may start with grants to anon and authenticated.
fix: Enable RLS on every table in an exposed schema, then add policies for exactly the access each role needs. Once RLS is on, the publishable key reaches no rows until a policy allows it, so write the policies before your app relies on the table.
affected: Supabase projects with any table in an exposed schema, usually public, that has RLS disabled
